{"self_assessment": "Impact: I owned the dorsal fin, the feature that makes the outline read as a fish and not just an oval. I took stroke four and branched it off the top line. After careful inspection I brought it to the point where it fell dark all the way out to the tip, so it falls with the start. Our final check showed about 122 of 125 dominoes connected, covering the body, both tail lobes and the fin.

Execution: I took the fin from start to finish. I inspected the joint closely several times and worked out where the chain was failing. I re-laid the stroke from the top line, then lifted the one jammed domino and bridged the gap with a connect. I made the call to leave the three stray dominoes under the fin standing, because they were invisible and pulling them risked disturbing a working joint. Once the fin was caught, I kept my hands off the table so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I confirmed my assignment out loud and told Priya I would stay clear of her end so we didn't crowd each other. I asked for the corner to be kept free while I worked, and I took Maya's and Leo's observations on the fin break and acted on them. I reported status as it changed (laid, pale, catching, dark to the tip) so Priya could run the final check with accurate information.

Leadership: I handed the final verification to Priya, kept the table calm in the closing minutes, and held to the hands-off agreement. I made clear, timely calls on the one open question at the end, which was whether to touch the strays.", "my_share_percent": 25}
